body: I would prefer it if the version of Jolt in godot does not diverge from the official Jolt release. This will make it harder to maintain it in the future. Instead of going adding a 'mForce' property, I would modify the 'mVelocity' directly in both the impulse and force case. The end result should be very similar. I have typed another comment   in apply_node_force to explain what this means.

So this could be:

`physics_vertex.mVelocity += impulse * physics_vertex.mInvMass;`

where

`impulse = force * last_step`

It's very debatable if dividing by mesh_vertex_count is the right thing to do or what applying a central impulse on a soft body even means. 

E.g.
* What if half of the vertices are pinned? This means that half of the impulse is applied to pinned vertices which is lost since they won't move, resulting in applying only half the impulse to the body
* What if the mass of the vertices is not uniform (I don't think this is currently possible)? Then some particles will accelerate less than others causing the body to stretch.

Maybe you should calculate the total delta velocity for the entire body by calculating p_impulse / total_mass_of_all_vertices and then applying that delta velocity to all vertices. Take care not to change the velocity of pinned vertices.

There is `void BodyInterface::AddForce(const BodyID &inBodyID, Vec3Arg inForce, EActivation inActivationMode)` but I'm realizing now that it has a bug because it applies the same force to all vertices (and thus applies too much force in total). I'll fix that.

> * What if half of the vertices are pinned? This means that half of the impulse is applied to pinned vertices which is lost since they won't move, resulting in applying only half the impulse to the body

So, like, the more vertices pinned, the stronger the impulse on the unpinned vertices. That felt kind of unrealistic, isn't it?

Edit: Using rigid body for example, If a rigid body is pinned on one side, apply_central_impulse() didn't only apply the impulse on the unpinned side, it still applies it in the center.

> What if the mass of the vertices is not uniform (I don't think this is currently possible)? Then some particles will accelerate less than others causing the body to stretch.

Wouldn't it just get pulled back together to prevent it from stretching too far.
I'm going to just use that function, even tho it's broken right now.

> So, like, the more vertices pinned, the stronger the impulse on the unpinned vertices. That felt kind of unrealistic, isn't it?

Yes that will be the case. The opposite is also weird. In any case, I think applying a force to the center of a soft body is just not very well defined. I played around with a few things and in the end I settled with the same as what you did as it is cheap and does what you want most of the time: https://github.com/jrouwe/JoltPhysics/pull/1412, you only need SoftBodyMotionProperties.cpp.

Edit: A previous PR that integrated a lot of Jolt's files has been merged now, so you can just update Jolt to the latest version now without generating any conflicts.
This newline change is not needed.
This newline change is not needed.
This wake_up call is not needed (JPH::EActivation::Activate below does the same thing).
I think you can implement this entire function in terms of apply_node_impulse. This will get rid of a bunch of duplicate code.
